description: Single-check mutants of the gateway journal: the frame accounting (a frame stream is the encoded TransportFrame), the data admission rule of the drain and cutover protocol and the transition guards of PR #227. The copy assembles the sources of the journal, the storage seam and the schema modules under one go.mod, because the module's own replace directives point outside its directory; every package keeps its repository-relative import path.

frame accounting: event ordinals need not be continuous
frame accounting: fragment descriptor count may overflow
frame accounting: bytes after the last event accepted
frame accounting: truncated manifest accepted
frame accounting: frame without data accepted
frame accounting: frame above the fragment bound accepted
frame accounting: chain sequence overflow ignored
frame accounting: event outside the manifest declared
frame accounting: PART frame measured with a maximal part index
frame accounting: COMPLETE frame measured as a PART frame
mutants.replacement: shape.Part = &proto.FragmentPart{PartIndex: frame, PartCount: entry.PartCount, FragmentTotalBytes: entry.FragmentTotal, Data: payload}

mutants.name: frame accounting: fragment count of the manifest ignored
mutants.original: return frameEncodedSize(&j.frameScratch, res.SequenceBase, entry, count, frame)

mutants.replacement: return frameEncodedSize(&j.frameScratch, res.SequenceBase*0+1, entry, count, frame)

lock around the release check removed
mutants.original:
j.mu.Lock()
	prefix, retired, err := j.checkReleaseLocked(id, manifestDigest, planDigest, maxKeys)
	j.mu.Unlock()
mutants.replacement: prefix, retired, err := j.checkReleaseLocked(id, manifestDigest, planDigest, maxKeys)
mutants.equivalent: The lock makes the check one step of the serialized writer. The check reads the store only and the storage seam serializes access on its own, so no test can observe its absence; the single-writer rule of the journal requires it.
